text: Fashion and beauty have the most buyers, but they are crowded and return-heavy. For a beginner, home & kitchen and jewellery look like the best starting points today: cheap, light to ship, no sizes, and few complaints.

headline: Women's ethnic: kurtis sell, sarees are heating up for festivals
text: Everyday kurtis are the volume sellers here, with far more reviews than sarees. Among sarees, bandhani, chunri and Banarasi designs are climbing ahead of Diwali and Chhath. Most sellers are manufacturers in Gujarat (Surat) and Rajasthan (Jaipur), so prices are already very low. Kurtis come in sizes, so returns are high. Sarees are free-size, which makes them the easier way into this category.

headline: Women's western: basic tops and shirts outsell dresses
text: Tank tops and crop tops sold as packs of 2 or 3, and plain women's shirts, carry most of the reviews. Dresses have many listings but fewer reviews each, so buyers are spread thin. Winter jackets and hoodies are showing up as new listings. Delhi sellers lead. Combo packs are the pattern that works here.

headline: Men's clothing: shirts sell, hoodies are the winter wave
text: Check and formal shirts are the proven sellers. Sweatshirts and hoodies fill the winter page now, but most are new listings with few reviews: demand is just starting, which is the moment to enter. Men's shirts draw the most 1-star reviews of any category, so quality complaints and returns are a real risk.

headline: Kids & toys: cheap clothing sets plus learning toys
text: Low-priced top-and-bottom sets are the biggest sellers. Educational toys such as practice books and flashcards sell strongly with very few complaints, and they have no sizes. Winter items (thermal sets, socks, sweaters) are rising. Prices here are the lowest of any category, so margins are thin.

headline: Home & kitchen: small, cheap, useful things win
text: Fridge covers, sticky wall hooks, agarbatti, wall stickers and evil-eye hangings are the steady sellers. Diwali items are rising right now: cotton diya wicks, tea-light candles, LED rope lights and decorative urli bowls. These items are light, have no sizes, and get few complaints. The festive window closes after Diwali, so plan the next season (winter, weddings) too.

headline: Beauty: biggest demand, but brands own it
text: Beauty has the most reviews of any category, but the leaders are brands (Mamaearth, Nivea, Muuchstac, Bella Vita, Dove). Reselling a brand needs the brand's authorisation, and making your own cosmetics needs a licence. Unbranded items that do well are body sprays, hair masks, silicone back scrubbers and lice combs.

headline: Jewellery: light, cheap and ahead of wedding season
text: American-diamond and rhodium necklace sets, jhumka sets, mangalsutra packs and bead necklaces lead. This category has one of the lowest complaint rates, items weigh almost nothing, and there are no sizes. Wedding season starts later this month, which usually lifts sets and maang tikkas. Gujarat and Maharashtra sellers lead.

headline: Bags & footwear: handbags are the core seller
text: Women's handbags and sling bags carry most of the reviews, followed by everyday flip-flops and slippers. New listings rising include heel-pad socks and men's wallets. Bags have no sizes; footwear does, and returns follow. Delhi sellers dominate bags.

headline: Electronics: earbuds sell most but break most
text: Wireless earbuds fill the listings, but they get the most 1-star reviews here, which means returns and penalties. Mobile holders and stands are cheap, steady sellers with fewer complaints. Speakers and USB fans also sell. If you try this category, start with holders and cable protectors, not earbuds.

headline: Health & fitness: pads lead, ear-lobe patches surprise
text: Branded sanitary pads (Everteen, Stayfree, Whisper) lead, which a beginner can't easily resell. Invisible ear-lobe support patches are a big unbranded hit, with very low prices and very few complaints. Footballs and badminton sets are rising as new listings for the winter sports season.

Jewellery sets and jhumkas, for the wedding season that starts later this month.
Diwali and pooja items (cotton wicks, tea-lights, rope lights, urli bowls), only if you can list within days, since Diwali is on 8 November.
Home utility items such as fridge covers, wall hooks and storage bags, which sell all year.
Kids' learning toys such as practice books and flashcards.
Women's handbags and sling bags.
Ear-lobe support patches and ear cleaners in health.
Avoid for now: earbuds (complaints), sized clothing (returns), branded beauty and pads (need authorisation).
